name: Request Attempt Closeout Backfill Plan
description: Make legacy token_use closeout projection automatic, bounded, and resumable without blocking startup or requiring user-run maintenance.

userStories.title: Extend backfill state schema
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want persistent per-batch backfill state so automatic legacy closeout projection can resume after crashes and restarts.
acceptanceCriteria: The state table has `cursor_created_at`, `cursor_token_use_id`, `started_at`, `last_run_at`, and `last_error` columns.
The migration preserves existing state columns and existing rows.
The migration is idempotent for already-migrated databases.

userStories.title: Add resumable bounded backfill cycle
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want one bounded backfill cycle that processes legacy token-use closeouts in small chunks and records progress after every batch.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a service entry point that processes at most `5` batches per call.
Each batch reads at most `1000` `app.token_use` rows.
The batch query includes `request_attempts_json IS NOT NULL`.
The batch query orders by `created_at, id` and resumes after the stored cursor.
The backfill captures a stable high-water mark for each run.
Each successful batch persists cursor, scanned, attempted, projected, batches, `last_run_at`, and clears `last_error` before the next batch starts.
The service sets `completed_at` only after the final eligible batch is processed.
Tests cover non-null filtering, cursor persistence, resume behavior, and completion.

userStories.title: Remove blocking startup backfill
userStories.description: As a user, I want the app to start without scanning historical token-use rows so startup stays fast as the database grows.
acceptanceCriteria: Startup no longer runs a full historical closeout rebuild or full historical closeout backfill.
Tests prove startup rollout cleanup does not trigger the full historical backfill path.

userStories.title: Add automatic backfill scheduler
userStories.description: As a user, I want legacy closeout projection to finish automatically in the background without running maintenance commands.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a scheduler that runs only in the DuckDB-owning maintenance runtime.
Each wake runs the bounded cycle with `1000` row batches and `5` max batches.
Failures are recorded in `last_error`, logged once for the wake, and retried on the next wake.
The scheduler does no work after `completed_at` is set.
The scheduler is registered automatically during server startup for the DuckDB-owning runtime.
The scheduler stops cleanly with the server process.
Tests cover runtime ownership guard, bounded work per wake, retry behavior, and completed-state no-op behavior.

userStories.title: Lock projection-only cleanup and writer projection
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want regression coverage proving cleanup stays fast and new token-use writes continue to populate closeout projection immediately.
acceptanceCriteria: `tokenUseQueryService.ts` continues to call `projectRequestAttemptCloseoutsForTokenUse` inside token-use insert transactions.
Tests prove new `token_use` inserts still create `app.request_attempt_closeout` rows immediately.
Tests prove stale cleanup releases leases through `app.request_attempt_closeout` projection only.
No required user-run maintenance command is introduced for correctness.
